premises.text: College students lack on-demand academic help and easy study-group/resource sharing, which widens the achievement gap
premises.evidence_span: It's really hard for students to master a topic if they can't get help on demand

premises.text: Study Room connects classmates via school email and course pages for collaborative study guides, section data, and free shared files across semesters
premises.evidence_span: any student can easily access the brainpower and knowledge of their entire class right on our platform

premises.text: Growth via campus founders plus first-day marketing, then student-to-student invites
premises.evidence_span: we put together a campus founder program, and we do a big marketing and social media push the first day of class

premises.text: Peer Mentor Program offers affordable on-demand one-on-one tutoring matched from platform students who know the course/professor/materials
premises.evidence_span: we're going to allow every single college student to offer online, on-demand tutoring sessions and make some money while helping others

value.text: College students get timely peer help and resources so they can master coursework (and aim for strong grades)
value.evidence_span: if they want to get a 4.0, go to getstudyroom.com

secondary_value.text: Peer mentors can earn money for college while helping others
secondary_value.evidence_span: a way for students to make some money for college

causal_links.evidence_span: Students learn best by helping each other out
That's how we were able to get over 40,000 students in just one semester
personalized one-on-one help right when they need it

notes: On-demand help, study-group, and resource-sharing pains folded as one student-support problem (§4.1.6). Course pages, collaborative guides, and file sharing folded as social-platform cascade (§4.1.7). Peer Mentor Program split as separately launched tutoring module with its own path to value. 40k users treated as traction evidence for campus GTM mechanism. Q&A line at end ignored (§4.2.5). Four-domain partition; not a need/product/money triad.
